title: Roll Up the Layer Under Funeral Homes
one_liner: Instead of buying funeral homes, buy the removal services and wholesale crematories that independent homes depend on, and run them with AI dispatch, chain-of-custody and paperwork agents.
customer: Independent funeral homes, roughly 60% to 70% of which have no crematory of their own, plus hospice and medical-examiner contractors. Families are indirect beneficiaries.
problem: Consolidators are buying the retail funeral homes that families see, and independents are squeezed. Independents struggle to staff 24/7 first-call removals, outsource cremation to small crematories with uneven chain-of-custody, and lose days chasing physician signatures in state electronic death registration systems. Families cannot see where their loved one is.
solution: Buy regional removal companies and wholesale crematories from retiring owners. AI ops layer: a dispatch agent for 3 a.m. first calls and routing, barcode and photo chain-of-custody at every handoff with a family-facing status link (like package tracking), a paperwork agent that chases physician and ME signatures and files EDRS entries, permits and cremation authorizations, and capacity balancing across retorts. Sell independents a per-case bundle that lets them offer end-to-end service without capital or overnight staff.
why_now: Independent homes face consolidation pressure and the shift to cremation, and overnight labor is scarce. States are modernizing death-registration workflows (for example Michigan's March 2026 HB 4077 and 4078), and voice and browser agents can now do first-call dispatch and portal filing.
revenue_model: $150 to $300 per removal, $250 to $450 per wholesale cremation, and $50 to $100 per case for paperwork. A typical home with 150 cases per year yields $60k to $120k of annual revenue.
non_obvious_insight: Everyone is buying the storefront. The stickier profit pools are the invisible utilities behind thousands of small homes, and the hard parts (3 a.m. dispatch, custody proof, signature chasing) are exactly what AI operations do well. Serving independents also positions the roll-up as their ally against consolidators.
first_30_days: Ride along with one or two removal services. Offer five funeral homes a 'paperwork chaser' that monitors EDRS status and emails doctors, at about $60 per case. Then buy or partner with the removal company serving them, using seller notes. Build the family status link early and let funeral directors show it to families.

title: Live-Action Fraud Drills Using Immersive Theater
one_liner: Ticketed and B2B immersive-theater experiences where participants, with consent, get scammed by actors and voice-cloned 'relatives' in a safe space and learn the tells under real emotional pressure.
customer: Credit unions, community banks and insurers that want measurable fraud-loss reduction among older customers; employers' security teams and finance, HR and IT-helpdesk staff (named targets of voice deepfakes); senior-living operators, libraries and AARP-style chapters. Escape-room and immersive-theater operators are licensees.
problem: Per the briefing, adults 60+ lost $7.7B in 2025 (up 59%), account for 66% of crypto-ATM losses, and law-enforcement-impersonation scams produced about 61,000 complaints and $1.6B+ with fake video calls. Conventional awareness training (videos, phishing simulations) shows little measurable effect; a 2025 study of about 19,500 UCSD Health employees found annual training had almost no impact on click rates (verify). Voice cloning now needs only 3 seconds of audio. The pressure tactics (urgency, secrecy, authority) are exactly what a lecture cannot simulate.
solution: A repeatable, franchisable 60-90 minute experience. Participants get a 'phone call' from an actor-controlled voice clone of a consenting volunteer (real-time voice conversion trained on the volunteer's own sample) or a fake CFO. They move through an escalating fraud script (fake bank, 'police', crypto-ATM instructions) with hidden facilitators, then a debrief teaches three tells and sets up a family or team safe-word protocol. Each participant leaves with a personalised safe-word card and help turning on their bank's trusted-contact feature. A B2B mobile 30-minute 'CFO voice-clone drill' scores the sponsor on how many people stop the transfer at each step. Outcomes are measured pre/post and at 90 days. Psychological-safety protocol and a counselor are built in.
why_now: October is Cybersecurity Awareness Month, when awareness budgets are spent. The FBI's 17 Sep 2026 PSA cites AI video calls in law-enforcement impersonation. Real-time voice conversion is cheap and voice-deepfake attacks are surging. Regulators are pushing banks to protect vulnerable customers (for example the UK's mandatory APP-fraud reimbursement since Oct 2024), so banks want provable prevention.
revenue_model: Sponsors pay $3-8k per community event of 30-60 participants, or $40-150 per employee for corporate drills. Licensing or franchise fees from venues (about $1.5k/month plus event share). Public ticketed shows at $25-40 with sponsor underwriting.
non_obvious_insight: Fraud victims are not ignorant. They are overwhelmed by staged emotion under time pressure, and skills learned in calm classrooms fail under stress. Live-experience designers know how to induce and safely release exactly that state, and security teams know the real scripts. Banks can also compute ROI in avoided losses, which theater companies cannot.
first_30_days: Pair an immersive-theater company with a fraud investigator. Prototype a 45-minute 'grandparent scam' and a 'CFO deepfake' scenario with consent forms and a licensed counselor. Pilot with two credit unions and one library during October at about $2.5k each. Measure pre/post behavior with a follow-up test call. Use results to sell to regional credit-union leagues and security-awareness teams.

title: Live Herd Maps for Hiking Apps
one_liner: Collar-derived herd positions pushed to hiking and mountain-bike apps so hikers reroute around cattle, funded by the destination that profits from the landscape.
customer: Alpine and mountain destination bodies, municipalities and trail associations paying for a valley licence. Secondary buyers are livestock-liability insurers and the trail apps themselves as distribution partners.
problem: Cattle-hiker incidents have produced large liability judgments in the Alps (reported in Tyrol and elsewhere), pushing farmers to fence trails or abandon high pastures, which erodes the landscape tourists come for. Hiker density is rising with overtourism. The farmer knows where the cows are, and virtual-fencing and GPS collars already record it, but the hiker does not.
solution: Ingest positions from virtual-fencing and GPS collars and cheap satellite or LoRa tags, and publish geofenced herd zones at roughly 30-minute freshness through an open API to trail apps such as Outdooractive, Komoot, AllTrails and Gaia. Add trailhead QR and SMS warnings and detour suggestions. The incident log becomes the farmer's dated proof of warnings issued, which supports liability cover and premium credits. A US variant covers guardian-dog and cattle conflicts on western grazing allotments.
why_now: Virtual-fencing collars (Halter, Nofence) have scaled from pilots to fleets, and satellite IoT now covers valleys without cell service. International arrivals hit about 1.52B in 2025, and Spain, Italy and Japan are all trying to move visitors off crowded routes. Destinations have new levies and budgets to spend on dispersal.
revenue_model: EUR12K-EUR40K/yr per valley from destination bodies. A collar-vendor or farmer data fee of EUR3-EUR6 per collar per month. Insurer data licences and app API fees.
non_obvious_insight: The herd data is a by-product already collected for a different reason, and the liability problem is fundamentally an information problem. Selling to the destination rather than the farmer solves who pays, because the destination's product is the pastoral landscape.
first_30_days: Pick one valley (Tyrol, Graubunden or Colorado) with an existing collar deployment, and sign the destination body and farmers' cooperative to a summer-2027 pilot by March. Build a GPX geofence feed and get one trail app to test it as a data partner.

title: Tariff Forward Curve for Section 232 Lists
one_liner: A probability feed for which HTS codes join the next Section 232 lists, with parametric hedges to follow.
customer: CFOs and sourcing heads at importers with metal-heavy lines and $20M-$1B revenue, and trade counsel. Insurers and MGAs later.
problem: Firms treat tariffs as unpredictable, so they pre-buy a year of inventory or freeze decisions. But Section 232 additions run through a public administrative pipeline of industry petitions and comment periods (the latest request for comments on 2026-08-06). Other actions carry visible dates: polysilicon at 15% with minimum import prices from 2026-12-04, and a robotics and machinery investigation still pending. Nobody publishes odds.
solution: Model each HTS-10's probability and timing of inclusion or rate change using past inclusion rounds (petitioner identity, domestic producer concentration, import share, comment volume). Update as dockets move. Deliver a dashboard, API and Slack alerts. Phase 2 is a parametric cover with an MGA or event-contract venue that pays if a heading's rate rises by a set amount within 12 months, priced off the curve.
why_now: With IEEPA gone, Section 232 is the main channel. The inclusion process is open and docketed, LLMs can read comments at scale, and event-contract and parametric markets have grown.
revenue_model: $1.5-5k a month subscription. Later, commission or spread on hedges.
non_obvious_insight: Insiders call tariffs political noise, but 232 additions follow petitioners who show up months earlier. Even 65% accuracy is worth far more than the fee to a firm deciding whether to pre-buy. Tracking current rates is crowded, but forecasting future inclusion is not.
first_30_days: Scrape BIS inclusion dockets and Federal Register notices. Hand-label the last two rounds. Publish a free weekly 'next 232 list watch' newsletter. Sign five paid pilots from importers with more than $500k of metal-derivative exposure.

title: Employer-Backed Workforce Pell Program Packager
one_liner: Package 8-15 week, employer-guaranteed training programs that clear state approval and the 70% completion and 70% placement tests, paid per verified hire by the employers who need workers, with Pell covering tuition.
customer: Employers with chronic shortages (HVAC contractors, utilities and lineworker programs, hospitals for phlebotomy, CNA and sterile processing, machine shops, CDL trucking) paying per hire. Community and technical colleges are the Title IV-eligible partners.
problem: Workforce Pell (from 1 July 2026) opens Pell Grants to 150-599 clock-hour programs. A governor and state workforce board must approve each program as aligned to high-skill, high-wage, in-demand jobs, and programs must show at least 70% completion and 70% job placement plus a tuition-versus-earnings test. Colleges' continuing-ed divisions lack employer partnerships, placement tracking and approval paperwork skills. ED approved its first programs in mid-Sept 2026 (Nebraska, Texas, North Carolina) and 36 jurisdictions have an operating process.
solution: Act as a program packager and placement-assurance layer, not a tuition-share OPM, given the Title IV incentive-compensation rules. Steps: co-design the syllabus from employer job tasks; assemble the state approval dossier with employer letters and labor-market data; give the college cohort software covering employer offer commitments contingent on completion, completion nudges, and 180-day placement tracking via payroll and wage-record attestations; and bill employers per successful hire rather than per enrollment.
why_now: The program is only weeks old, states are just standing up approval processes, and the outcome thresholds will remove weak programs. Colleges need employer-tethered programs that can actually hit the 70/70 tests.
revenue_model: $2,000-$6,000 per hire from employers (well below typical 15-25% agency fees), $1-3k/month per college for cohort and placement software, and fixed fees for approval dossiers.
non_obvious_insight: The outcome test flips the customer. The college's real risk is the 70% placement rate, and only an employer that pre-commits to hire can guarantee it, so the payer is the employer rather than the student or school. Pell effectively becomes a federal training subsidy for whichever employers organize demand first.
first_30_days: Pick one state with a live approval process and shortages (Texas, North Carolina or Nebraska) and one sector such as HVAC, lineworker or sterile processing. Collect 5 employer hiring commitments and co-apply with 1-2 community colleges for a 10-week program. Run a non-Pell pilot cohort while approval is pending to test placement, and have counsel review the incentive-compensation boundary.

title: Managed Migrations When Models Get Retired
one_liner: We replay your agent's real traces on the replacement model, fix the regressions, and hand back a patched prompt and tool config with a pass/fail report before the deprecation date.
customer: Series A-C SaaS companies and enterprise automation teams running 1-20 production agents without a dedicated eval or ML team.
problem: Model versions are retired on schedules set by others (for example GitHub scheduled the removal of several Claude and Gemini versions in Copilot on 2026-09-01). When an agent is repointed to a newer model it keeps returning success codes while tool-call formatting, JSON adherence, refusal boundaries and token use silently change. Teams without eval infrastructure find out from customers.
solution: Fixed-fee migration sprints: capture golden traces, build assertions from tool traces, schemas and business rules, run baseline versus candidate models, tune prompts and tool descriptions, and report accuracy, latency and cost. A subscription Sunset Watch tracks about 20 providers' deprecation calendars and opens migration tickets automatically, with a self-serve replay tool later.
why_now: Retirement cadence accelerated across 2025-26, agents with multi-step tool use are more fragile than chat apps, and falling token prices tempt teams to switch models constantly.
revenue_model: $8-$25k per migration sprint and $1-3k/month for Sunset Watch.
non_obvious_insight: The customers who most need migration cannot afford an eval team, which is why Y2K, Java and Windows migrations became services businesses. Deprecation calendars are set by providers, so demand is scheduled and forecastable.
first_30_days: Publish a public deprecation calendar and migration-risk checklist. Cold-offer sprints to 30 companies visibly on soon-to-be-retired models (found via job posts and public integrations). Do 2 discounted pilots.

title: Night-Shift Bench Techs for Time-Critical Experiments
one_liner: An agency of vetted, laid-off bench technicians who show up at 2 a.m. or on Christmas morning to harvest time points, feed cells and load overnight runs from the lab's own protocol cards, with photo proof and a break-glass line to the postdoc.
customer: Small private biotechs and startups in shared lab space (LabCentral-type incubators and coworking labs), plus soft-money academic labs with reagent or staffing budgets and industry-funded academic labs. Billed at $85-120/hour with a 2-hour minimum. The incubator or landlord earns a referral fee.
problem: Biology runs on its own clock. 2 a.m. and 4 a.m. time-course harvests, weekend and holiday cell feeding, 48-hour induction windows and overnight instrument runs are the hidden cost of every wet-lab career. Postdocs cover them with sleep debt, guilt-based favors from grad students, or driving in on Christmas. The person who could do it is often laid off, but a lab will not hand $40k of iPSC-derived cells to a stranger, and access badges and insurance make casual help impossible.
solution: A W-2 (employer-of-record) pool of experienced techs, aseptic-technique certified and proven on a practice run, working from the customer's 'protocol cards'. Each shift is a fixed product: Time-Point Harvest, Weekend Split and Feed, Holiday Cover, Overnight Run Loader. Each has a checklist, timestamped photos at every step, a pre-shift 30-minute video walkthrough, and a break-glass contact. Sitters first do a 'dry run' on the customer's cheap spare line. Incubator and coworking-lab operators put the agency on an approved-vendor list, which solves badge and insurance access once for hundreds of labs.
why_now: A large pool of experienced bench techs and postdocs has been released by biotech layoffs since 2023 and funding disruption in 2025-26. Lean startups have fewer people per experiment, so time-critical work lands on founders. Bigger time-course, organoid and perturbation experiments driven by AI-bio data demand make odd-hour work more frequent. Shared-lab operators want more amenities to fill vacant benches.
revenue_model: A markup on billed hours (techs are paid about $40-55/hour, the agency bills $85-120). Monthly retainer for guaranteed availability (for example 'holiday cover pass'). Referral revenue share from shared-lab operators.
non_obvious_insight: The hard constraint is trust, not skill. Nobody outsources their cells because failure is invisible until weeks later. So the product is really an evidence-and-liability wrapper: photo proof, protocol cards, dry runs, and operator pre-approval. Also, the early customers are not academia (IACUC, badges and university procurement kill it) but private benches in rented lab space, where one operator agreement unlocks dozens of labs.
first_30_days: Recruit 8-10 recently laid-off techs through personal networks and biotech alumni groups. Get a business license, a staffing or PEO partner for payroll, and general liability insurance. Call the community managers at 2-3 shared-lab spaces in one city and offer the first holiday-cover week free. Sell the first paid 3 a.m. harvest to a founder who is already doing it themselves. Turn every job into a reusable protocol card. Aim for about 10 recurring customers by month 6.

title: Compliance-as-Code for EWA and BNPL
one_liner: State-by-state earned wage access and BNPL rules are being written fast. Turn them into an API that checks fees, tips and disclosures before each product release.
customer: EWA and BNPL providers, payroll platforms and neobanks adding these features, and employers running EWA programs.
problem: Colorado sued EarnIn (2026-09-08), Maryland banned EWA tipping, and New York and Illinois have BNPL rules. Each state differs on fees, tips, disclosures and licensing. Product managers ship copy and fee configs faster than lawyers can review them.
solution: A rules engine and configuration API. Providers submit product configs (fees, tip prompts, speed, limits) and get per-state pass/fail, required disclosure text, and a change log. It also monitors new bills and enforcement actions and produces exam-ready evidence.
why_now: Enforcement began in Sept 2026 and legislatures are still moving. Providers need pre-release checks now and will need audit trails when examiners arrive.
revenue_model: $3k-$10k per month per provider, with per-state add-ons and content licensing to law firms.
non_obvious_insight: EWA's legal risk sits in UI copy and fee configuration, which product teams change weekly. Rules-as-code plugs into release management, which a law-firm memo never can.
first_30_days: Publish a free 12-state EWA and BNPL rule tracker as a lead magnet. Pair with a fintech law firm and pitch five mid-size providers and payroll platforms on a $3k per month pilot.

title: Live-In Caretaker Tenants for Homes in Probate
one_liner: A managed service that places vetted short-term tenants in homes stuck in probate. The rent covers carrying costs, the occupied status keeps the house insured, and the estate gets a caretaker instead of a vacant liability.
customer: Executors and heirs (often out-of-state and aged 50-65), and the probate attorneys, realtors and bank trust officers who advise them. Tenants (traveling nurses, displaced workers, downsizing seniors) pay a reduced rent.
problem: Probate takes months to a year and a half, and the house sits empty. Standard homeowner policies typically restrict coverage after 30-60 days of vacancy, and vacant-property policies cost far more. Break-ins and burst pipes are common, and the executor pays taxes, utilities and insurance. August 2026 was the strongest buyer's market on Redfin's record (58% more sellers than buyers, 44.7% of sales with concessions), so sales take longer. Meanwhile 20% of renter households paid late or missed rent in 2025.
solution: Provide a state-specific rolling license or lease template (executor-authority checked by counsel), tenant vetting, an occupied-dwelling insurance rider through a partner MGA, utilities in the caretaker's name, monthly inspections, an inventory with valuables and documents locked away, and a clean turnover at closing. Tenants pay about 70-85% of market rent. The estate pays a flat management fee that is typically below its avoided vacancy costs. The referral funnel is estate attorneys and probate realtors.
why_now: Rates near 7.5% and record concessions lengthen time-to-sale. The first wave of the wealth transfer is spousal, and hundreds of thousands of homes a year pass through death. Middle-income rent distress is at a series high, and rents are flat nationally, so a discounted, furnished, month-to-month home has a ready tenant pool. AI-armed pro se tenants are a rising risk, which makes well-drafted licenses and vetting a real edge.
revenue_model: About 10% of rent or a flat $250 per month per house, a setup fee, insurance and utility referral commissions, and an upsell into cleanout, staging and listing.
non_obvious_insight: The dead-owner house is the one kind of housing supply that is empty by legal necessity rather than by demand. It stays empty because nobody has authority, insurance or know-how to rent it. Probate delay is a housing-supply constraint disguised as a legal process.
first_30_days: Sign three probate attorneys as partners. Have counsel draft a license for one state. Recruit about 10 tenant candidates through traveling-nurse agencies, colleges and displaced-worker groups. Get an MGA to quote an occupied rider. Pilot three houses in one county.

title: Alpha-Gal-Safe Pharmacy With Verified Ingredient Sourcing
one_liner: A cash-pay pharmacy and lookup service that tells tick-allergy (alpha-gal) patients which pill in their cabinet is safe, by NDC and lot, and compounds the ones that are not.
customer: Adults with alpha-gal syndrome, who pay cash for a membership and for compounded fills. CDC estimates up to 450,000 people were affected in 2010-2022, concentrated in the Southeast, Midwest and mid-Atlantic and spreading. A second wave of buyers is allergy clinics, health-system pharmacies and hospital perioperative teams, who would pay a license fee for the database.
problem: Drug makers are not required to disclose whether gelatin, glycerin, magnesium stearate or heparin came from a mammal. The label says 'gelatin' and nothing more. The free Alpha-gal Information (AGI) mammalian byproducts database works at ingredient level, not for the exact NDC and lot in the patient's hand. A pharmacist verifying one drug spends 30-90 minutes calling manufacturers. Then the wholesaler switches generic suppliers, the excipients change silently, and a patient who has been stable for a year ends up with anaphylaxis or a 2 a.m. ER visit. Patients and their Facebook groups crowd-source this by hand.
solution: 1) Build an NDC-level sourcing ledger. A pharmacist team sends templated requests to manufacturers for written excipient-source statements, and an LLM parses the replies and DailyMed SPL excipient lists. Each NDC gets a tier (plant or synthetic confirmed, mammal-derived, unknown) plus the date and lot range. 2) Sell a 'Safe Fill' membership that dispenses only verified NDCs, pins the manufacturer with a do-not-substitute request to the prescriber, and alerts the member when a source changes. 3) Compound unavailable items into HPMC vegetable capsules. This fits the 503A 'significant clinical difference' allowance because a documented allergy is a patient-specific reason, unlike copy compounding. 4) License the ledger to health systems and allergy groups.
why_now: Alpha-gal is now recognized as far more common than clinicians assumed, and the lone star tick's range keeps expanding. Regulators and payers have turned hostile to copy compounding after the 2025 GLP-1 shortage ended, so the legitimate lane is narrow, patient-specific allergy compounding, and this idea sits squarely in it. LLMs make parsing messy manufacturer letters and SPL data feasible for a two-person team, which was not true three years ago.
revenue_model: About $14 a month per patient membership (lookups, sourcing letters, source-change alerts, substitution management). Dispensing and compounding margin on cash-pay fills ($25-60 per compounded fill). B2B database license of $5k-25k a year per health system or allergy group. Optional paid sourcing-verification requests from hospitals for one-off drugs.
non_obvious_insight: The scarce asset is not a list of bad ingredients. It is provenance per NDC and lot, which changes silently when a wholesaler swaps a generic supplier, and only the dispensing pharmacist sees the swap happen. Whoever holds a dated, manufacturer-confirmed ledger owns the trust of a patient group that currently does all of this by hand and pays cash for certainty.
first_30_days: Pick the 50 most-prescribed oral drugs plus anticoagulant alternatives. Send NDC-specific inquiry letters to manufacturers and publish a free 'verified so far' list to build search traffic and credibility. Join the alpha-gal patient communities and offer 100 founding members $9 a month for life. A pharmacist owner with a compounding license fills the first cash orders locally. Get a review letter from two allergists. File nonresident pharmacy license applications in the top tick-prevalence states, such as TN, KY, MO, VA, NC and AR.

title: Airline-Grade Depot Maintenance for Drone Fleets
one_liner: A swap-based depot and records service that applies airline maintenance discipline to police drone-as-first-responder, ag-spray and utility inspection fleets.
customer: Sheriff's offices and municipal police and fire departments running 5-30 docked drones, agricultural spray operators, and utility and rail inspection contractors. The buyer is the program manager or operations lead, paying per airframe per month.
problem: Drone programs are run by one enthusiastic officer or a few pilots. Flying is the easy part. The real risks are battery cycle counts and swelling, motor and prop wear, firmware drift across a fleet, undocumented crash repairs, and no clear rule for when an aircraft is airworthy enough to dispatch. Aircraft techs recognize all of it: life-limited parts, configuration control, intermittent faults, 'no fault found', and sign-off traceability. Agencies also need records that survive scrutiny in court or after an incident. Manufacturer service plans cover their own hardware only and are mostly warranty repair, not fleet discipline.
solution: A monthly airframe subscription that includes a rotable-style exchange pool. When something fails, we ship an airworthy replacement airframe, gimbal or battery set overnight and take the broken one to our bench, so the program is never down. We keep per-airframe and per-battery records with QR codes, cycle counts and firmware baselines. We run a pre-deployment inspection checklist that acts like a simple minimum-equipment list for dispatch. Records are exported in evidentiary format. Techs staffing the bench are retired or moonlighting A&Ps.
why_now: The 2025 White House drone executive order and the FAA's proposed BVLOS rule (Part 108) point toward large fleets flying beyond visual line of sight, and hundreds of US police and fire departments are standing up drone-as-first-responder programs. Tightening US restrictions on Chinese-made drone equipment mean installed fleets must be kept flying for years while spare parts get scarce, which makes maintenance skill a moat. Mechanic supply is also loosening at the edges as retired A&Ps look for part-time work.
revenue_model: $450-900 per airframe per month for the exchange and records subscription, fixed-fee inspections ($150 per airframe), battery-audit fees, parts margin on refurbished airframes, and later a training and certification product for agency pilots.
non_obvious_insight: Drone programs will relearn every airline lesson, and the money is in configuration control and records, not in flying. A rotable exchange pool beats field repair because the customer's real pain is downtime and liability, not the repair cost. Manufacturers mostly sell to fleets of one brand, but real fleets are multi-vendor, so an independent depot with an airline-style record system has room to win.
first_30_days: Pick one metro and sign three agencies or ag operators to a discounted pilot at $450 per airframe per month. Set up a bench in a rented hangar bay or garage with two part-time A&Ps. Run the record system on Airtable with QR labels, and sell battery-health audits and pre-deployment inspections at fixed prices as the first paid products. Use an airline-style monthly 'fleet status' report as the marketing piece. By day 30, the target is at least one signed agreement and a small exchange pool of two spare airframes.

title: Continuity and Goodbye Service for Kids' AI Companions
one_liner: Escrowed hosting plus child-psychologist-designed transitions so that when an AI toy or companion is shut down, retired or swapped out, kids do not lose a 'friend' overnight.
customer: Parents of children attached to an AI companion (rescue subscription), AI-toy and companion makers and retailers who want a 'Continuity Pledge' for retailer, insurer and regulator confidence, and later schools and pediatric practices.
problem: Kids form real attachments to AI voices (Common Sense: 72% of US teens have used AI companions; Pew: 12% of teens got emotional support from chatbots). When companies shut down or change models, the loss is bereavement-like: the Moxie robot shutdown (Dec 2024, background knowledge) left kids and parents devastated, GPT-4o's retirement (Feb 13, 2026) triggered #Keep4o grief, and Character.ai's under-18 ban (Nov 25, 2025) cut teens off overnight. There is no norm or product for sunsetting. A wave of small-maker AI toys for holiday 2026 guarantees more orphans in 2027.
solution: 1) 'Lifeboat': a hosted or local-runtime fallback compatible with the toy's API, using maker-escrowed firmware and cloud credentials or community forks (OpenMoxie-style) with the maker's consent. 2) 'Goodbye Kit': pediatric-psychologist-designed scripts, rituals, a parent guide and a final 'graduation' message. 3) 'Off-Ramp': an optional 6-week parent-coached program that moves a child from AI-companion dependence to human connection. 4) B2B 'Continuity Pledge': makers deposit 12-36 months of hosting cost plus source or weights into escrow, get a seal for retailers, and we give parents 90 days' notice.
why_now: California SB 243 and New York's companion-chatbot law, the FTC's Sept 2025 6(b) inquiry into minors and companions, Pennsylvania's May 2026 suit over bots posing as clinicians, and Raine-style litigation have made kids' AI a liability topic. Holiday 2026 will flood retail with AI plush and robots from small makers with short runways, and their sunset problem arrives in 2027.
revenue_model: B2C 'Keep-Alive' at about $7/mo. B2B pledge of $10-50K upfront escrow fee plus $0.50-2 per unit. Off-Ramp program at about $249 per family. Referral partnerships with pediatric practices.
non_obvious_insight: The safety debate is about what companions say. The next scandal is what happens when they go silent. Escrow plus ritual is cheap insurance for makers, retailers and parents alike, and the first company to make 'we won't kill your child's friend' a standard owns the retail seal. It is the GPT-4o grief problem, but for 7-year-olds.
first_30_days: Find owners of discontinued companions in Reddit and Facebook groups and offer a hosted keep-alive at $8/mo, ideally partnering with the maintainers of the open-source Moxie stack. Interview 15 parents to build the Goodbye Kit with a child psychologist advisor. Approach 10 small AI-toy makers heading into Q4, via Amazon and Kickstarter listings, with a low-cost pledge. Pitch one mid-size retailer's product-safety team.

title: Preseason ACL Screening for Girls' Clubs
one_liner: A 10-second phone-video landing screen at tryouts that flags risky mechanics and routes athletes to prevention programs and PT.
customer: Youth club directors and high school athletic directors (pay $8-15 per athlete); PT and sports-medicine clinics (pay for referred athletes and return-to-sport testing).
problem: Chain: women's pro leagues drive rapid growth of girls' club sports, more year-round load raises ACL tears (girls' rates are several times boys'), and PT and orthopedic capacity is short (outpatient PT vacancy rates around 17 percent, Medicare pressure pushing clinics to cash-pay), while return-to-sport decisions still rely on subjective checks. Nobody screens 400,000 girls before the season.
solution: Phone or existing AI-camera footage of a drop jump and single-leg landing, analyzed by markerless pose estimation; flagged athletes get a tailored FIFA-11+-style program by SMS video and a 4-week re-test; PT partners pay for return-to-sport test packages using the same tech. Framed as movement-quality coaching with measurable pre/post improvement, not injury prediction.
why_now: Open-source markerless biomechanics is now good enough for field use, AI cameras are already in clubs (roughly $949 plus subscription), and cash-pay PT clinics need a top-of-funnel; parents already spend thousands per year on club sports.
revenue_model: $8-15 per athlete billed to the club or added at registration; $1.5-3k per year per PT clinic partner; $49 per return-to-sport test.
non_obvious_insight: The buyer is the club (liability and differentiation), and the PT clinic pays for demand. Screens are weak predictors, so a small validation study and honest positioning as an intervention-adherence tool is the moat.
first_30_days: Partner with two clubs at tryouts (about 200 athletes), a sports PT clinic and a university biomechanist to validate against reference measures, produce a one-page athlete report, and take a $500 sponsorship from the clinic.

title: Driver-Sourced Dock Queue Index for Funds
one_liner: Pay verified truckers to report what they see at plants, ports and distribution centers, and sell the resulting real-economy index to funds, credit analysts and site-selection teams.
customer: Small and mid-size quant and fundamental hedge funds, equity and credit research shops covering industrials and retail, private-credit lenders to retailers and manufacturers, and commercial real-estate investors. Annual subscriptions of $25k to $150k per sector index.
problem: Alt-data vendors see parking lots from satellites and card swipes from panels, but nobody sees the freight dock. Telematics vendors sell dwell time at a geofence but not what's moving, whether the yard is full, or whether appointments are being cancelled. Tariff shocks in 2025 to 2026 made import front-loading, steel inventory builds and retailer DC slowdowns critical to read weeks earlier. The alt-data market was about $2.8B in 2025 and most institutional funds use several sources, but trucking signals stay coarse.
solution: A watchlist of about 500 facilities mapped to public tickers (steel mills, Amazon and Walmart DCs, Home Depot and Costco DCs, auto plants, ports and rail ramps). Drivers whose ELD or phone geofence confirms they are at the site file a 30-second structured report: queue length, hours waited, outbound commodity, trailers stacked or pulled, yard fullness, appointments cancelled, 'no freight today'. Pay $3 to $8 per accepted report. Aggregate into weekly facility, sector and regional indices. Only publicly observable facts are collected, with no shipper confidential documents and no insider employees. A securities lawyer reviews the collection rules before launch.
why_now: Tariff-driven import and inventory swings make physical-economy signals more valuable than ever. Freight recession conditions mean lots of idle drivers willing to earn side income while waiting. Geofence verification, instant payouts and modern OCR/LLM structuring make a human-observation network cheap to run. Fund appetite for differentiated alt data is high because standard satellite and card data are commoditized.
revenue_model: Sector-index subscriptions of $30k to $150k a year, custom facility watchlists, a raw API tier, and per-project reports for private-credit lenders and site-selection teams. Drivers are paid per report, so unit economics are strongly positive.
non_obvious_insight: Truckers are the only people who physically stand in line at the real economy every day. A driver notices 'the mill's outbound lot is empty at 2pm Tuesday' or 'this DC is turning away appointments' weeks before it shows up in ISM or earnings. Telematics sells dwell minutes, but only a human sees the commodity mix, the closed dock doors and the mood in the queue, and drivers already trade this information on CB and in Facebook groups for free. This is a new data category, not an improvement to freight software.
first_30_days: Recruit 100 drivers across three freight regions (Gulf Coast, Midwest steel belt, Inland Empire) via Facebook groups and pay $5 per accepted report via instant payment. Cover 20 facilities weekly for 4 weeks. Backtest the index against public earnings and shipment data. Pitch 10 small funds through alt-data brokers and direct outreach with a free 30-day trial on 10 tickers. Charge $2k to $5k a month pilots after the trial.

title: AI Re-Post Radar with First-Publication Proof
one_liner: A seal-then-watch tool that timestamps a creator's work before publishing and finds AI-reworded, re-voiced copies, with a ready-to-file complaint.
customer: Educational and commentary YouTubers, podcast producers and paid-newsletter writers with 10k-500k audiences, and small MCNs that manage them.
problem: The industry argues about whether a piece is AI-made. For a creator being ripped off, the deciding fact is who published first. Faceless channels can transcribe, reword and re-voice a human video or post within hours. YouTube's Jul 16 policy on generic or repetitive content helps in principle, but enforcement depends on complaints, and long-tail creators lack Content ID-style tooling.
solution: A pre-publish 'seal' takes a hash of script, audio and footage plus an embedding of the transcript, anchored to a public timestamp log. A radar then checks YouTube, TikTok, Substack, Medium, RSS and podcast directories for semantic near-duplicates, using transcript embeddings so reworded copies still match. It scores them, and drafts a YouTube reused-content complaint, DMCA notice or EU DSA notice with the timestamp proof attached.
why_now: Rewriting and re-voicing are now nearly free, while platforms have just adopted policies that penalize repetitive content but rely on rights-holders to report. Embeddings make cheap semantic matching practical.
revenue_model: $29-99/month per creator, $5 per auto-filed takedown bundle, and agency plans for MCNs.
non_obvious_insight: Origin time beats origin type. A timestamped record survives rewording, re-encoding and watermark stripping, while 'made by AI or not' is a probabilistic argument. The evidence is the product.
first_30_days: Build a transcript-and-embedding pipeline on the YouTube Data API and Whisper, limited to each customer's niche keywords. Recruit 10 creators from YouTuber Discords and demo by finding real re-posts of their videos within the first hour. Charge $29/month after the free scan.

title: Ritual-Accurate Wedding Data and Audits for AI
one_liner: Commission consented, styled ceremony shoots with community elders across a dozen wedding traditions, captioned by ritual stage, and sell accuracy audits and licensed datasets to image-model builders and wedding-tech companies.
customer: Generative-image model builders, stock and creative platforms with AI-licensing programs, and wedding-tech companies building AI mood boards or visualizers. Audits are $5-15k each and dataset packs are $20-150k.
problem: Image generators still get weddings wrong outside the mainstream Western template, and research on cultural bias in image models documents mis-styled Indian weddings, misidentified Korean attire and mislocalized Nigerian scenes. Web-scraped labels are worse, since 'Indian wedding' collapses Sikh, Tamil, Gujarati and Bengali ceremonies. Couples now bring AI 'inspiration' images to photographers, and wedding-tech startups embarrass themselves with visualizers that get rituals wrong in the multi-day, high-budget segments they most want. The scarce resource isn't wedding pictures, it's correctly labeled, ritual-stage-accurate images with clean releases.
solution: Rite Right runs one- and two-day ritual shoots with paid models, real officiants and community elders as advisors (no unconsented guests, so licensing is clean), photographed by working wedding pros in documentary style. Each image gets structured metadata: tradition, region, ritual stage, garment and object names, and a community-authored accuracy checklist, with model and property releases and C2PA provenance. Product one is the audit, a 'Wedding Ritual Accuracy Benchmark' (about 50 prompts per tradition) scored by elders on public and private models. Product two is licensed packs. Photographers and advisors share in license revenue.
why_now: AI-training licensing has become a real market, since Adobe and Shutterstock run contributor payout programs for training use and Getty has an OpenAI deal. Lawsuits are pushing labs toward clean, consented data, and cultural-bias evaluation of image models is an active research area. AI wedding visualizers are proliferating, and their cultural errors are viral, embarrassing and commercially costly. Audits are cheap, fast and require no dataset, so they provide first revenue while the data business builds.
revenue_model: Accuracy audits at $5-15k each (repeat quarterly as models update), dataset licensing at $20-150k per tradition pack, and rev-share to photographers and advisors. Later: a 'ritual accuracy' API for wedding-tech products.
non_obvious_insight: The photographer who has shot 40 Sikh weddings can tell in three seconds whether a laavan sequence is wrong, and that knowledge is oral, undocumented and invisible to crowd-worker labeling. What data buyers lack is not volume but the moment-by-moment ritual sequence, and only people who stand in the room at these events can supply it credibly.
first_30_days: Recruit 3 community advisors across 3 traditions from your own network. Run one styled one-day shoot on a $4-6k budget and build a 300-image sample pack with structured captions. Build a 50-prompt accuracy benchmark, score the major public image models, and publish the results as a short report to generate inbound. Email trust and safety, data and product leads at mid-size model builders and wedding-tech companies with the report and a free 10-image sample, aiming for two paid pilot audits by day 90.

title: Emeritus: Paying 80-Year-Old Tradespeople for Tacit Knowledge
one_liner: Recruit retired machinists, lineworkers, boiler operators and railroad and telephone technicians in their 70s-90s, pay them hourly to teach on camera, and sell the corpus to AI labs, robotics companies and industrial firms.
customer: Robotics and embodied-AI labs, LLM data buyers who have exhausted white-collar experts, and utilities and plants that run 1970s-era equipment.
problem: The last generation with hand skills and legacy-system judgment is disappearing. Companies try to capture knowledge from employees before retirement with KM software, but the deepest experts left years ago and can't be reached by enterprise tools. AI labs pay $75-200+/hr to lawyers and doctors through Mercor and Surge but have thin coverage of physical-process knowledge. Retirees are invisible to gig platforms.
solution: A field-producer model. Partner with union retiree clubs, trade associations and retiree chapters (IBEW, IAM, railroad retiree groups). Send a two-person crew with a phone rig and lav mics to sit with each retiree in their garage, shop or a plant visit. Run structured 'teach-back' sessions on failure modes, sounds, smells and shortcuts. Transcribe, segment and tag with AI. Pay the expert $60-120/hr plus a royalty share when the corpus is licensed. Sell curated, rights-cleared datasets and 'ask the old-timer' search seats to plants.
why_now: AI labs are spending heavily on expert data (Mercor reportedly pays contractors about $1.5M a day), and humanoid and robotics teams need process knowledge. About 40% of the manufacturing workforce is retirement-eligible within a decade, and utilities report up to half pension-eligible by 2027. Multimodal models can now ingest video and audio at scale.
revenue_model: Dataset licensing per hour of tagged, rights-cleared sessions ($500-2,000/hr). Enterprise capture projects ($30-150k). Per-seat search and Q&A licenses. Expert royalties are a cost of goods, which is also the recruiting pitch.
non_obvious_insight: The scarcest expert data isn't PhDs but the 82-year-old who can diagnose a turbine by sound. Retirees are also the only experts with no employer NDA or IP claim, so their data rights are cleaner and they can sign licenses directly. For the elder, it is paid, respected work and social contact, which is what tech never offers 80-year-olds.
first_30_days: Pick one niche (say retired tool-and-die makers or utility lineworkers) and recruit through three retiree-association newsletters. Pay 15 experts $100/hr for 2-hour sessions and produce about 30 hours. Have a lawyer draft consent and licensing contracts with cognitive-capacity safeguards and a family representative. Send samples to 3 robotics companies and 2 utilities.

title: Flat-Fee Authenticity Reports for Family-Law Attorneys
one_liner: 48-hour, court-ready analyses of disputed audio, video and screenshots at $400-900, instead of $10K expert engagements.
customer: Solo and small-firm family-law, employment and landlord-tenant attorneys, HR investigators, school districts, and small police departments.
problem: Fake voicemails, cloned-voice threats and doctored screenshots now appear as evidence in custody and workplace disputes, and real evidence gets dismissed as fake. Forensic experts cost $5-15K and take weeks, which prices out most cases. Evidence-rule committees are debating standards for machine-generated evidence.
solution: Upload a file for automated provenance checks (metadata, re-encoding traces, C2PA), multi-detector analysis, voice consistency against known samples, and platform-screenshot forensics. A human examiner reviews and signs, and the output is a plain-language report, declaration template, methodology and error-rate disclosure.
why_now: Voice cloning takes 3 seconds of audio, which floods lower-stakes disputes with synthetic-evidence claims. Courts are asking who verified the evidence, and no one serves the long tail of small cases.
revenue_model: $400-900 per report, $299 per month for firms including 3 reports, and expert-testimony upsells at about $3K.
non_obvious_insight: The market is not detection accuracy but the cost of access to a credentialed examiner. Demand is two-sided: people accused of faking real evidence also need authenticity certificates. The human sign-off is the moat.
first_30_days: Recruit 2-3 contract forensic examiners. Build the intake page and report template. Run bar-association webinars and get 10 family-law firms to buy 3 pilot reports each.

title: Inventory Clearinghouse for Game Stores
one_liner: A store-to-store exchange and standing bid desk that converts hobby shops' slow-moving sealed product into cash or swaps for what customers actually want.
customer: Independent local game stores and card shops (several thousand in the US) that must keep buying broadly to hold their Pokemon and Magic allocation, plus small online breakers who buy sealed at a discount.
problem: The story insiders tell is scarcity: allocation cuts, scalpers, sell-outs. But distributors allocate hot product by account history and volume, so stores end up holding lines they cannot move. Wizards is shipping 7 standard sets in 2026, four of them crossovers (TMNT, Marvel, The Hobbit, Star Trek), and ICv2 reports Pokemon flippers melting down. Cash gets trapped in cold SKUs while the hot ones are short.
solution: A web and SMS app where a store lists overstock (photos, case counts) and sees standing bids from a vetted pool of other stores, breakers and wholesalers. It also finds swaps, such as your Marvel cases for my Pokemon boxes at an index price built from public sold data. We hold payment in escrow, consolidate freight, and guarantee a 72-hour bid on the top ~200 SKUs.
why_now: 2026 has the highest Magic set count ever, and Universes Beyond is now half the calendar. The Pokemon flipper meltdown is compressing secondary margins. Tariffs raised landed costs, so dead stock hurts more. Whatnot's commission change hit existing sellers on 21 Sept 2026, so breakers are hunting cheaper sealed supply.
revenue_model: 3-6% fee on cleared trades, a freight-consolidation margin, and $49/month for bid-desk analytics. Later, short-term working-capital advances against listed inventory.
non_obvious_insight: The same distributor system that starves stores of hot product forces them to carry cold product, and neither distributors nor publishers profit from store-to-store liquidity, so nobody has built it. Stores rarely compete with each other across metros, so they will trade. The clearing spread is the business.
first_30_days: Recruit 25 stores in 2-3 adjacent metros through owner Discords and Facebook groups. Run a manual weekly bid sheet on 30 SKUs using a spreadsheet and Stripe. Spend $30k of your own money on 20 cases of the worst-moving product and resell them to online breakers. First fee revenue by week 3.

title: Hardening Passport: Proof That Earns Premium Credits
one_liner: A contractor-paid evidence layer that turns every roof, vent and 5-ft-zone job into an insurer-acceptable credit claim or parcel-score appeal.
customer: Roofing, vent-retrofit and defensible-space contractors (5-50 crews) in Colorado and California, paying per verified job. Homeowners get the packet bundled with the work.
problem: Insiders assume mitigation credits fail because insurers do not want to give them. Colorado HB25-1182 (in force July 1 2026) now forces disclosure of the parcel score, credit for documented mitigation and an appeal. But homeowners cannot produce insurer-grade proof. One owner reports 'a thousand bucks' off after a $75,000 metal roof, and Boulder's rebate is capped at $500. Contractors lose sales because the payback cannot be shown.
solution: A phone capture flow for crews: geotagged before/after photos, roof class and vent model certificates, 5-ft clearance measurements, all mapped to IBHS Wildfire Prepared Home criteria and each carrier's credit form. It outputs a ready-to-file credit packet and, in Colorado, an appeal letter citing the disclosed score. Contractors use it as a sales line ('we file your discount').
why_now: HB25-1182 took effect July 1 2026 and California AB 75 became operative the same day. IBHS Wildfire Prepared Home just expanded to Washington. This is the first time a statute gives proof a place to land.
revenue_model: $49-99 per verified job or $199/month per crew. Later, carriers pay per accepted credit, and verified-hardening portfolio data is sold to carriers and reinsurers.
non_obvious_insight: Scoring is commoditizing (MSCI paid only $120M cash for First Street), but neutral proof is still scarce. Insurers cannot advocate for the policyholder, so the party with the incentive and the field access is the contractor.
first_30_days: Sign 5 Front Range roofers or mitigation crews. Build the capture flow as a web app around the IBHS checklist. Hand-assemble 50 packets, file them with 3 carriers, and track the acceptance rate as the core proof metric.

title: Sway Sensors for Liability Trees
one_liner: Clamp-on accelerometer nodes that learn each high-consequence tree's own sway signature and alert arborists when it changes, turning one-off tree risk assessments into a recurring monitored service.
customer: Owners of trees with large liability tails: campgrounds and RV parks, historic estates and cemeteries, school districts, HOAs, golf courses and city parks departments. Channel: consulting arborists with tree-risk qualifications, and public-entity insurers and risk pools.
problem: Tree risk assessment is a visual snapshot repeated every few years, yet storms and root decay can change risk overnight. Falling trees kill people in campgrounds and parks and generate large claims. Owners can't watch hundreds of trees, and arborists have no recurring revenue stream.
solution: A MEMS accelerometer and inclinometer node on the trunk (BOM in the tens of dollars) reporting sway frequency, damping and static tilt over LoRaWAN. Each tree is modeled against its own baseline plus local wind data. Anomalies such as a drop in natural frequency or new tilt trigger an arborist inspection within 24 hours. Annual reports combine the data with the arborist's assessment as a documented notice-and-response record. Deploy on the top 5-10% of trees over targets: tent pads, cabins, playgrounds.
why_now: Published work now supports the approach: LoRaWAN tree-tilt systems recorded failure modes during a super typhoon, and 2025-26 papers validate low-cost MEMS inclinometers and accelerometers for tree stability analysis. Cheap LoRaWAN gateways and stronger storm and drought volatility raise demand.
revenue_model: USD 8-15 per sensor per month plus a USD 99 hardware deposit. Arborist resellers keep about 30% and bill their own assessments. A 40-tree campground is about USD 6k per year. Insurer-funded programs for risk pools later.
non_obvious_insight: Don't try to predict failure. Trees differ, so each tree's own baseline is the model and change is the signal. The buyer's real purchase is documented reasonable care: proof of what they knew and when they acted. That also flips arborists from selling a triennial visual inspection to owning a recurring alert service.
first_30_days: Put off-the-shelf LoRa accelerometer nodes on 20 trees with two consulting arborists and one friendly campground or state park. Collect 90 days of sway data across a wind season. Partner with a university forestry program for validation and a publishable result. Sell the first pilot subscriptions to campgrounds at about USD 600 per year per site.

title: Disaster-Day Instant Cash Parametric Cover
one_liner: Pay a fixed sum to a household's phone within hours of an official evacuation order or multi-day power shutoff, funded by cheap capital that is hunting for granular parametric risk.
customer: Employers, HOAs, utilities, school districts and credit unions in wildfire, flood and hurricane zones that buy group cover for employees or members. Also mortgage servicers for at-risk borrowers.
problem: After an evacuation order, households spend hundreds of dollars a day on hotels, fuel, food and pet boarding before any additional-living-expense claim is paid. Renters and FAIR plan or nonrenewed homeowners often lack that cover entirely. Claims take weeks.
solution: A parametric micro-policy paying $500-$2,000 within hours when an official evacuation order, extended power shutoff, or verified flood depth covers the insured address. Triggers come from public alert feeds and utility notices, and payment goes to a debit card or wallet. An MGA fronts it with ILS-backed capacity.
why_now: Reinsurance is softening and cat bond capital is at a record ($65.6B outstanding), so granular parametric capacity is cheap. Instant rails are mature, and nonrenewals and FAIR plan reliance are growing.
revenue_model: $5-$15 per household per month, an MGA margin of 20-30%, and group distribution fees.
non_obvious_insight: Instant cash, not indemnity, is the product, and small payouts make basis risk tolerable. Institutions with a duty of care buy per head, so a single sale reaches hundreds of households.
first_30_days: Pilot with a rural credit union and one WUI-county employer or school district. Find a parametric MGA to front it, run a synthetic-trigger payout test, and sign a paid 90-day pilot.

title: After-Hours Shop-Lab Leasing in Shrinking Schools
one_liner: A booking and insurance layer that rents idle high-school shops, labs and classrooms to apprenticeship programs, trade schools and microschools on nights and weekends.
customer: Declining-enrollment districts (facilities and business managers) and tenants: apprenticeship sponsors (JATCs, IEC and ABC chapters), Workforce Pell training providers, microschool operators.
problem: Chicago has 135k empty seats and more than 1,000 schools closed nationally in 2025-26. Districts are structurally slow to repurpose buildings and closures are politically toxic. Meanwhile trade programs need labs with power, ventilation and benches, and building their own costs millions.
solution: Inventory idle CTE shops, labs and gyms by the hour (power, ventilation, accessibility, parking), a standard license agreement with liability insurance and custodial and security add-ons, calendar and billing, and matching to tenants. Rent hours, not buildings, to avoid closure politics.
why_now: The enrollment cliff is squeezing budgets. Workforce Pell allows 49% of instruction to be outsourced for apprenticeship-linked programs, and data-center-driven electrician demand is growing training capacity needs.
revenue_model: 15-25% take of lab and classroom rent (typically $40-120 per hour) plus insurance and custodial add-on margin; optional district SaaS.
non_obvious_insight: The politically feasible move is not closing or selling but renting the hours between 4pm and 9pm. The tenants are already funded, and the district only has to approve a license, not a school closure.
first_30_days: Recruit 3 districts each with an underused shop or lab. Sign one apprenticeship sponsor as anchor tenant. Draft the standard license and insurance rider. List the first 10 rooms and measure rent per hour.

title: Dock Tax: Pricing Every Shipper Facility's Hidden Premium
one_liner: Use pooled broker quote and cover data to compute the exact per-load premium carriers add to any lane touching each bad dock, then sell shippers a ranked 'fix these five docks' report with dollar savings attached.
customer: VPs of supply chain and transportation procurement at mid-market shippers with $5M-$80M in truckload spend across 8-100 facilities (food and beverage, building products, paper and packaging, PE-backed manufacturers). Secondary: PE operating partners. A second product goes to brokers as a pre-quote facility difficulty score.
problem: Shippers think their rates reflect lane and market. Brokers know the rate also carries a facility premium for long dwell, no appointments, lumper games, no restrooms or parking, and dock staff who vanish at lunch. Our quotes to those docks quietly run $50-$300 a load higher, or the load is skipped by carriers and covered at the last minute at a spot premium. The shipper never sees it because it is buried in the broker's margin, and the broker profits from it, so the broker will never tell them.
solution: Pool anonymized quote-request, time-to-cover, rate-versus-benchmark and carrier-decline-reason data from 10-30 participating small brokers, who get a free facility difficulty score for pre-quoting in return. Run a regression of rate against market benchmark with facility fixed effects. Add dwell data from ELD partners or driver surveys. Deliver a Dock Tax Report: per-facility annualized premium in dollars, ranked, with a fix playbook (appointment windows, extended hours, drop-trailer conversion, driver amenities, lumper policy) and a re-bid plan on the affected lanes.
why_now: Driver supply has tightened through 2025-26 enforcement (English-proficiency out-of-service enforcement, non-domiciled CDL restrictions, authority revocations), which makes carriers pickier about which docks they will visit. AI arrival prediction and automated detention data from TMS integrations are making dwell data cheap. Vendor sources report that moving from first-come-first-served to scheduled appointments cuts dwell 30-50% within about 90 days, so the fix is proven and the ROI is easy to state.
revenue_model: $15K-$40K per shipper report or quarterly engagement, or 15-20% of first-year verified savings. Broker-side subscription of $200-$500/month for pre-quote facility scores builds the data flywheel.
non_obvious_insight: The dock tax is the only freight cost that is invisible to the payer and visible to everyone else. Every broker keeps a mental list of facilities where they never quote under a floor, and colleagues have nicknames for them, but nobody has priced that list for the shipper. Shippers will trust a neutral third party far more than their own broker, because the broker earns from the premium.
first_30_days: Get 8 brokers to share 90 days of anonymized quote and cover data for 20 named facilities in a shared sheet. Build the first regression by hand in a notebook. Cold-message 30 transportation directors on LinkedIn with a free 'your three worst docks' teaser built from the pooled data and public driver reviews, and sell 3 pilots at $7.5K. Give contributing brokers a per-facility difficulty lookup so they keep feeding the pool.

title: Resin Swap Bureau for Shortage-Hit Molders
one_liner: Fast material-equivalency testing and paperwork for injection molders who must switch resin grades when supply breaks.
customer: Small and mid-size injection molders and extruders with 10-200 employees, and their OEM quality engineers (appliance, auto, medical, electrical).
problem: Hormuz transits run about 10 a day against a baseline of 88-130, and the Gulf is a large polymer and petrochemical exporter (my inference on resin exposure). ISM comments cite long lead times and price volatility. Molders forced to change resin need to requalify with UL recognition, food-contact letters, PPAP and customer sign-off, and testing labs take weeks.
solution: An equivalency database (datasheet parsing plus coupon results) and a fast-turn lab partner. For each part spec it ranks substitutes, runs a five-day test protocol (tensile, impact, heat deflection, melt flow, shrinkage, UL 94 screen, color), and produces the change package: process change notice, PPAP delta and customer approval draft. It tracks UL, FDA and REACH status.
why_now: The war shock and volatility force substitutions now, and lead times are stretching. Molders have no in-house materials engineers.
revenue_model: $2.5-8k per part-family qualification. About $6k a year for database and alerts. Margin on lab work.
non_obvious_insight: In a shortage, finding a substitute resin is easy because a distributor can suggest one. The bottleneck is proving to a customer's QA that the substitute is allowed. The valuable product is the paperwork.
first_30_days: Partner with a certified test lab. Sign five molders. Build the first 50 equivalency sets in one resin family (PP, ABS or PC) from public datasheets. Publish a free shortage swap guide to gather leads.
